name: Respiratory variants & flu
summary: Early H1N1 flu season: US flu admissions up 27% in a week; no WHO variant of concern
state: US flu hospital admissions rose 27% in a week and the CDC reported the season's first child death, in an early season driven by a drifted H1N1 strain (Medical Daily; CDC FluView). In England, UKHSA's 29 Oct report showed flu GP swab positivity rising to 11.0%. Health systems are not reported as strained, and no WHO variant of concern had been designated as of 6 Nov.
for_you: In the UK, the NHS offers free flu vaccination to eligible groups, including over-65s, young children and people with long-term conditions; check NHS guidance. Older adults and young children are most at risk of severe illness.
rubric_hit: Northern Hemisphere flu season unusually early; no variant of concern or health-system strain (Watch)

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
